{{DISPLAYTITLE:Similarities to ''Sword of Truth''}}
{{Spoiler_page|''{{Wlink|sot|Sword of Truth series|The Sword of Truth}}'' and ''{{Wlink|sot|Legend of the Seeker}}''}}
{{Quote|I'm aware of Mr. Goodkind.|Robert Jordan<ref>[[Source:USA Today Interview, 6 January 2004]]</ref>}}
== Introduction ==

This page is intended to contain a comprehensive list of all commonalities between ''The Wheel of Time'' and the late Terry Goodkind's ''Sword of Truth'' series.

{{SimilaritiesDisclaimer}}

That being said, it merits addressing the commonly held belief that the ''Sword of Truth'' borrowed heavily from ''The Wheel of Time'' with some of the words of the people involved.

{{Quote|For Richard Scholten, I have never discussed anything whatsoever with Terry Goodkind. I suggest that you check the publication dates of his books and mine. Of course, he says he has never read me, or so I'm told, and I would never contradict a statement like that. Just check out the pub dates on his books, and the pub dates on mine, those that contain the similarities you speak of.|Robert Jordan<ref>[[Source:Blog - NO CHAMPAGNE YET, 14 July 2006]]</ref>}}

{{Quote|Wizard's First Rule was actually a very solid book, and though I didn't get into the second, I can see why people enjoy reading him.|Brandon Sanderson<ref>[https://www.theoryland.com/intvmain.php?i=622 Q148, Reddit AMA 2011, Aug 31 2011]</ref><ref>[https://www.reddit.com/r/Fantasy/comments/k0fp8/comment/c2gm1hr/ Brandon Sanderson Reddit AMA (2011)]</ref>}}

{{Quote|Heh. Line from Towers of Midnight said: "And Rand did such and such." Brain keeps reading "Ayn Rand." Did Goodkind sneak over and rewrite my manuscript?|Brandon Sanderson<ref>[https://www.theoryland.com/intvmain.php?i=45 Q58, Twitter: TOM Writing and Editing Process, 28 July 2010]</ref>}}

{{Quote|[Robert Jordan] also said that Terry Goodkind actually uses WOT as inspiration, instead of going to a historical source. He sounded serious.|Mark Erikson<ref>[https://www.theoryland.com/intvmain.php?i=106 Q7, 27 Aug 1999]</ref>}}

== Story and events ==
* Early in the first book, an angry mob of locals accosts [[Moiraine Damodred|Moiraine]]/[[Bran al'Vere|Bran]] / {{Wlink|sot|Kahlan}}/{{Wlink|sot|Zedd}} because of Moiraine's/Kahlan's magical abilities, only to be dispersed by Moiraine's story and the arguments of Bran/[[Haral Luhhan]] and Zedd.
* The R-named protagonist begins life in the western region of his continent before departing east for his adventure, eventually reaching a desert far to the east where his father was/is the most powerful single leader.
* A resurgent empire (mostly serving the role of villains) comes up from the south to challenge the protagonist and the main characters.

== Characters and creatures ==
* The [[Creator]] and the {{Wlink|sot|The Creator|Creator}} have the same name and role and (near-total) silence in both series.
* The [[Dark One]] and the {{Wlink|sot|The Keeper|Keeper}} have obvious similarities to each other and to the embodiments of evil of various religions. Both were locked away by the Creator.
* The [[Keeper of the Chronicles]] and the Keeper share a name. Incidentally, the loyalist Keeper for most of the series was the head of the [[Black Ajah]] and one of the highest-ranking servants of the Dark One.
* [[Rand al'Thor]] and {{Wlink|sot|Richard Rahl}}
** Protagonists and the prophesied Chosen One who will lead the forces of the Light against the forces of evil.
** Similar stature and age
** Both begin the series as "normal" men but become arguably the most powerful magic-user in the world.
** Both are adopted and raised by a man, with their mothers dying when Rand/Richard was young.
* [[Thom Merrilin]] and {{Wlink|sot|Zedd}}
** Physically somewhat similar - thin, white-haired
** Perform a similar mentor role to [[Rand al'Thor|Rand]]/{{Wlink|sot|Richard}}
** Generally kindhearted, but very capable of violence and a degree of ruthlessness
** Thom is a magician and one of the finest [[Gleeman]] in the world, Zedd is one of the most powerful wizards in the world.

== Locations ==
* The [[Spine of the World]] and the mountain ranges separating the {{Wlink|sot|Westland}}/{{Wlink|sot|Midlands}} from {{Wlink|sot|D'hara}} have a similar location and orientation, and produce similar isolating effects on the neighboring civilizations (though in the latter case the [[w:c:Boundaries|Boundaries]] are the dominant factor)
* The [[Stone of Tear]] has obvious nominal similarities to the name of the {{Wlink|sot|Stone_of_Tears_(item)|Stone of Tears}} magical item, which lends its name to the {{Wlink|sot|Stone_of_Tears|second book}} (published 1995, over five years after [[The Eye of the World]]).
* The [[White Tower]] and the {{Wlink|sot|Palace of the Prophets}} are the fantastical headquarters of a female-only order of very long-lived magic users. Both contain repositories of prophecy.

== Magic and artifacts ==
* The ''[[A'dam|a'dam]]'' and (to a lesser extent) [[Domination Band]] have obvious similarities to the {{Wlink|sot|Rada'Han}} "seamless" collars used by the {{Wlink|sot|Sisters of the Light}}.
* [[Dreamwalking]], while used very, very differently, appears in both works and is called by the same name. Egwene and others are [[Dreamwalking|Dreamwalkers]]. {{Wlink|sot|Jagang|Jagang}} is a {{Wlink|sot|Dream Walker}}.
* {{A|red-rod}}The red rod ter'angreal (a "brilliant red rod no larger than [Elayne's] forefinger"{{ref/book|10|21}}) is visibly similar to, if smaller than, the {{Wlink|sot|Agiel|Agiel}} (a "small leather rod") used by the {{Wlink|sot|Mord-Sith}} to torture people. ''(Note: This is almost certainly coincidence or a (very, very unlikely) possible Jordanian reference to'' Sword of Truth'', since {{Wlink|sot|Wizard's First Rule}} was released many years before {{8}}.)''
* The {{Wlink|sot|Additive Magic}} and {{Wlink|sot|Subtractive Magic}} dichotomy bears a very superficial similarity to the pairing of the [[Creator|creative]] [[One Power]] and the destructive [[True Power]] (or, to a lesser extent, ''[[saidar]]'' and ''[[saidin]]'').

== Peoples and institutions ==
* The [[Aes Sedai]] and the {{Wlink|sot|Sisters of the Light}}
** Both are female-only orders of long-lived magic users.
** Both are largely isolated, but do travel the world, mostly as individuals or small groups.
** Both are headquartered in a fantastical fortress.
** The Aes Sedai hunt down and gentle men who can channel. The Sisters hunt down and collar (male) wizards.
** Both contain within them a covert fifth column serving the embodiment of evil: the [[Black Ajah]] and the {{Wlink|sot|Sisters of the Dark}}.
* The [[Seanchan]] and the {{Wlink|sot|Sisters of the Light}} both collar magic users and justify it by the dangers posed by the magical abilities.
